name: finding-format
description: Produce traceable candidate and verified findings with independent severity, impact, likelihood, priority, and provenance fields.

# Finding Format

Specialists emit candidates; they do not decide production impact or score.

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "SEC-C001",
  "identity": {
    "defect_key": "stable-kebab-case-defect-kind",
    "primary_location": "path/file.py",
    "symbol": "optional stable symbol",
    "profile_rule_id": "optional canonical profile rule",
    "anchor_id": "optional deterministic anchor id"
  },
  "category": "security",
  "title": "Short factual title",
  "claim": "Precisely scoped, falsifiable claim",
  "severity": "critical|high|medium|low|informational",
  "technical_quality_impact": "systemic|material|localized|none",
  "profile_rule_id": "optional canonical rule from the selected profile",
  "likelihood": "high|medium|low|unknown|not_applicable",
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "rationale": "Concise evidence interpretation",
  "impact": "Concrete consequence if verified",
  "evidence": [
    {
      "type": "source|graphify|tool|test|configuration|documentation|dependency_vulnerability",
      "path": "path/file.py",
      "start_line": 10,
      "end_line": 24,
      "content_hash": "sha256:...",
      "fact": "What the evidence directly establishes"
    }
  ],
  "counter_evidence": [],
  "standards": [],
  "recommendation": "Proportionate action"
}
```

After verification and production-impact classification, the final finding follows `finding.schema.json` and independently records:

- `severity`: `critical|high|medium|low|informational`
- `technical_quality_impact`: `systemic|material|localized|none`
- `production_impact`: `blocker|required_before_production|post_release|none`
- `likelihood`: `high|medium|low|unknown|not_applicable`
- `remediation_priority`: `P0|P1|P2|P3|P4`
- `verification_status`: `supported|partially_supported|unsupported|inconclusive`
- `identity`: normalized defect key, primary location, symbol, profile rule, and deterministic anchor
- `fingerprint`: SHA-256 generated by `finding_identity.py`; agents never invent this value

These fields are not aliases. Severity measures the consequence of the verified problem. Technical-quality impact measures how broadly it degrades design/code health and drives category penalties. Production impact drives release actions. None mechanically implies another.

Use `profile_rule_id` only when the finding directly satisfies a rule in the resolved profile. The rule's default technical-quality impact is a starting point and must be narrowed or raised from evidence. Unsupported and inconclusive findings use both `technical_quality_impact: none` and `production_impact: none`.

A supported or partially supported non-informational finding represents a real defect and must use at least `localized`; `technical_quality_impact: none` is invalid even when `production_impact` is `none`. If no technical-quality consequence can be established, narrow it to an informational observation or reject/mark it inconclusive.

Every supported negative finding requires structured evidence provenance. High/Critical findings require source or deterministic tool evidence, or Graphify plus source confirmation. Graphify-only observations remain candidates. A named CVE requires `dependency_vulnerability` evidence with package/version, advisory ID, and tool/advisory source.

Use the same `defect_key` for the same defect across runs. In baseline revalidation, copy the baseline identity/fingerprint when the claim is the same even if its title is reworded. Once written to `verified-findings.json`, identity, fingerprint, and immutable semantic fields may not change during synthesis.
